title: Break-even point
summary: How much you need to sell to cover every cost, and how much to earn what you want.

gross-sales.label: Gross sales
gross-sales.placeholder: Sales for the period including taxes (e.g. 1118000)

variable-costs.label: Variable costs
variable-costs.placeholder: Cost of goods consumed in the period (e.g. 270000)

fixed-costs.label: Fixed costs
fixed-costs.placeholder: Salaries, charges, rent, utilities, expenses, amortization and fees (e.g. 313977)

desired-profit-before-tax.label: Desired profit before tax
desired-profit-before-tax.placeholder: Monthly profit you want, before income tax (e.g. 200000)
desired-profit-before-tax.hint: If you think in take-home terms, divide it by (1 − 0.35).

steps.tax-rate: Tax rate = gross sales ÷ net sales = {grossSales} ÷ {netSales} = {taxRate}
steps.variable-cost-rate: Variable cost rate = variable costs ÷ net sales = {variableCosts} ÷ {netSales} = {variableCostRate}
steps.break-even: Break-even point = fixed costs ÷ contribution rate = {fixedCosts} ÷ {contributionRate} = {breakEvenNetSales}
steps.target-sales: Net sales for your profit = (fixed costs + profit before tax) ÷ contribution rate = ({fixedCosts} + {desiredProfitBeforeTax}) ÷ {contributionRate} = {targetNetSales}
steps.target-gross-sales: Gross sales = net sales × tax rate = {targetNetSales} × {taxRate} = {targetGrossSales}

manual-break-even.title: Handbook data, with $200,000 profit before tax

errors.taxes.must-not-exceed-gross: Taxes can't be equal to or greater than gross sales.
errors.variable-costs.must-not-exceed-gross: Variable costs must be lower than net sales.
